comment_data.body:
I assume you're not pressing `g?` fast enough, so the neovim motion is triggered instead (`:h g?`). "Fast enough" means within the time set by `vim.o.timeoutlen` (which is 1000 ms by default).

The help window should appear when you do the following:

```vim
:lua MiniFiles.open()
:lua MiniFiles.show_help()
```

`g` keymaps are tricky to deal with. For example, remapping `g?` in normal mode should behave the same way:

```lua
vim.keymap.set("n", "g?", function()
  vim.print("Did you press me?")
end)
```

---

The easiest solution is to increase the `vim.o.timeoutlen` option. You can even set it temporarily while the explorer is open, but this feels a bit off:

<details><summary>No warranty</summary>

```lua
local files_au = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("minifiles", { clear = true })
local timeoutlen
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
  pattern = "MiniFilesExplorerOpen",
  group = files_au,
  desc = "Change `vim.o.timeoutlen` after openinig `mini.files`",
  callback = function()
    timeoutlen = vim.o.timeoutlen
    vim.o.timeoutlen = 1000
  end,
})
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
  pattern = "MiniFilesExplorerClose",
  group = files_au,
  desc = "Restore `vim.o.timeoutlen` after closing `mini.files`",
  callback = function()
    vim.o.timeoutlen = timeoutlen
  end,
})
```

</details>

---

You can also solve the problem by using `mini.clue`:

<details><summary>Example</summary>

```lua
vim.pack.add({
  { src = "https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim" },
})

vim.o.timeoutlen = 200

require("mini.files").setup()
vim.keymap.set("n", "<Space>e", MiniFiles.open)

local files_au = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("minifiles", { clear = true })
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
  pattern = "MiniFilesBufferCreate",
  group = files_au,
  callback = function(e)
    if MiniClue then
      -- Should this be the default?
      MiniClue.ensure_buf_triggers(e.data.buf_id)
    end
    -- local buf_map = function(mode, lhs, rhs, opts)
    --   vim.keymap.set(mode, lhs, rhs, vim.tbl_extend("keep", opts or {}, { buffer = e.data.buf_id }))
    -- end
    -- buf_map("n", "g?", MiniFiles.show_help, { desc = "Set cwd" })
  end,
})

local miniclue = require("mini.clue")
miniclue.setup({
  triggers = {
    -- { mode = { "n", "x" }, keys = "<Leader>" },
    -- { mode = "n", keys = "[" },
    -- { mode = "n", keys = "]" },
    -- { mode = "i", keys = "<C-x>" },
    { mode = { "n", "x" }, keys = "g" },
    -- { mode = { "n", "x" }, keys = "'" },
    -- { mode = { "n", "x" }, keys = "`" },
    -- { mode = { "n", "x" }, keys = '"' },
    -- { mode = { "i", "c" }, keys = "<C-r>" },
    -- { mode = "n", keys = "<C-w>" },
    -- { mode = { "n", "x" }, keys = "z" },
  },
  clues = {
    -- miniclue.gen_clues.square_brackets(),
    -- miniclue.gen_clues.builtin_completion(),
    miniclue.gen_clues.g(),
    -- miniclue.gen_clues.marks(),
    -- miniclue.gen_clues.registers(),
    -- miniclue.gen_clues.windows(),
    -- miniclue.gen_clues.z(),
  },
})
```

</details>

---

@drowning-cat, as previously noted my setting of `timeoutlen` to 400 is the cause of my issue.

But with regard to  the `mini.clue` solution: I am using `mini.clue`. Its `setup`  creates a `BufWinEnter` autocmd that calls `ensure_buf_triggers`. Also, why `vim.o.timeoutlen = 200`?  In any, erm, event, thanks for taking time on this! By happenstance I currently have an intense interest in the internals of `clue.lua`.

> Its `setup` creates a `BufWinEnter` autocmd that calls `ensure_buf_triggers`.

It is deliberately not ensuring triggers in 'mini.files' buffer or any non-listed buffers except some [allowlist](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/402ee6c6ec8ea44b22330446c8fb4e615fd3953e/lua/mini/clue.lua#L1171-L1174).

If you have any questions on this, feel free to open a new discussion. May I ask why the interest?

Couple of extra questions:

- Does executing `:lua MiniFiles.show_help()` while inside the explorer work?
- Does executing some other buffer-local mappings work? Like after you navigate inside some subdirectories, does pressing `<BS>` show explorer at its anchor (initial path used to open an explorer)?

After `:set timeoutlen=1000` I can use `g?` successfully.
